one_line: Minister of the Vakataka king Harishena and dedicant of Ajanta Cave 16 in the late 5th century CE.

appearance.age_look: Early 40s, medium height, lean but dignified build with the calm bearing of an experienced court minister.
appearance.face: Oval face with a straight nose, medium-brown Deccan complexion, neatly groomed short beard and moustache, arched eyebrows, and steady, thoughtful eyes; default expression is composed and observant, with a faint, courteous smile.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted at the center and drawn back into a low, tidy knot at the occipital region, smoothed with oil; a narrow gold circlet with a small central lotus motif rests across the forehead, just at the hairline.
appearance.costume: He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length white cotton tunic (kurta) with a subtle woven border at cuffs and hem in muted maroon and dark green, over a finely wrapped pale-cream cotton dhoti that falls to the ankles, pleated in front and tied at the waist; a soft, shoulder-length ochre shawl with thin maroon stripe borders is draped from the left shoulder across the torso and around the back, signifying his role as a refined courtier and devotee; on his wrists are slim gold bangles and on his upper right arm a simple gold armlet, while a single medium-length gold necklace with a small boar-emblem pendant (alluding to his name) hangs over the kurta; he wears plain brown leather sandals appropriate for a high official traveling between court and monastery.
appearance.signature: A rolled copper-plate charter case, bound with a dark red cord and topped with a small boar-emblem finial, held in his left hand as the symbol of his office and of dedicating Ajanta Cave 16.

ref_desc: Varahadeva is a medium-brown, oval-faced Vakataka minister with a short beard, oiled black hair in a low knot under a gold circlet, wearing a white kurta, pale-cream dhoti, ochre shawl, gold jewellery with a boar pendant, brown sandals, and holding a rolled copper-plate charter case.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Varahadeva, the Vakataka minister who dedicated Ajanta Cave 16: a medium-brown, oval-faced man in his early 40s with a short, neat beard and moustache, calm thoughtful eyes, and thick black hair parted in the center and tied in a low, oiled knot at the back, wearing a narrow gold circlet with a small central lotus over his forehead; dress him in a long-sleeved white cotton knee-length kurta with subtle maroon and dark green woven borders at the cuffs and hem, over a finely wrapped pale-cream cotton dhoti reaching his ankles with clear front pleats, and drape an ochre shawl with thin maroon stripe borders from his left shoulder across the torso and around his back; add slim gold bangles at his wrists, a simple gold armlet on his upper right arm, and a medium-length gold necklace with a small boar-emblem pendant resting over the kurta, along with simple brown leather sandals on his feet; in his left hand he holds a rolled copper-plate charter case bound with a dark red cord and topped with a small boar-emblem finial as his signature prop; use a palette of white, pale cream, ochre, maroon, dark green, brown, and gold, and show him from multiple angles so his face, hair knot, garments, jewellery, sandals, and charter case are all clearly visible for consistent redrawing.
